resources.string: A walnut hi‑fi, a needle, the crackle of vinyl
A silver tape deck, winding, the hiss of tape
A hundred million songs in your pocket, and hardly one heard all the way through. Here it’s the old way: one album a week, a whole side at a time, and the record wears in as you love it.
The whole app follows: how it looks, how it sounds, and what skipping a song does.
You can change it later in settings.
The shop gets a delivery once a week. A week you don’t use doesn’t carry over.
The shop gets a delivery once a week. A week you don’t use doesn’t carry over.
Side A, turn it over, side B. No shuffle, no playlists.
Side A, eject, turn it over, side B. No shuffle, no playlists.
Move the needle while it’s down and the record keeps the mark, and clicks there each time round. Lift it first and it’s fine.
A cassette can’t jump: it winds, at the speed of a real deck. A skip in another player creases the tape.
When it’s full, one record goes to the second‑hand shop, with a farewell line.
When the rack’s full, one cassette goes to the second‑hand shop, with a farewell line.
The first three are a gift
For the records you already own and love.
For the albums you already own and love.
Start with three records you already love: the shop gives them away.
Start with three albums you already love: the shop gives them away.
Records you let go. Each one can be bought back, as that week’s buy.
Cassettes you let go. Each one can be bought back, as that week’s buy.
Delivery’s in: one record this week
Delivery’s in: one cassette this week
One record a week, and an unused week doesn’t carry over. Put others aside on the counter for later weeks.
One cassette a week, and an unused week doesn’t carry over. Put others aside on the counter for later weeks.
What’s playing in your streaming app. You listen there; the record lives here.
What’s playing in your streaming app. You listen there; the cassette lives here.
From a folder on the phone
Your own files. Played here: needle, crackle and all.
Your own files. Played here: tape hiss, wow and all.
No music found in that folder.
An album you’ll play in another app.
To see what your player is playing, Side A needs notification access. It reads only the song, never your notifications.
Start an album in your player and it shows up here.
It waits for a later week.
From the folder: %1$s, %2$s. Plays here on the turntable.
From the folder: %1$s, %2$s. Plays here in the tape deck.
Plays in your streaming app; Side A listens along, learns the songs and keeps the record.
To bring this one home, another goes to the second‑hand shop. Which one?
To bring this one home, another goes to the second‑hand shop. Which one?
A line to remember it by. It keeps its notes and its marks.
The music folder can’t be reached any more. Was it moved?
It waits on the counter until a week with a free buy.
It can be bought back in a week with a free buy.
The songs appear as the record plays.
The songs appear as the tape plays.
Take it back to the shop
Where you were, what it brought back. In a year you’ll find it here.
Rain, the night train, that summer…
Let your ears rest. Put the phone down. The music is about to start.
The phone was picked up. Put it down and just listen.
Tap the lever by the arm (or the button) to raise and lower the needle. Drag the arm to move it; with the needle down, that scratches the record.
Winding takes as long as on a real deck. ⏏ turns the cassette over.
Turn it over to side B
Both sides played. Sit a moment in the quiet.
Start “%s” in your player, from the first song.
No player to ask. Open it once, then try again.
Skipping a song in the player scratches the record.
Skipping a song in the player creases the tape.
Your shelf stays the same; only the room changes around it.
The day each week the shop has something new.
A pause to rest the ears before an album.
Picking up the phone lifts the needle
Picking up the phone stops the tape
Leave the app with the screen on and the music pauses. With the screen off it plays on.
Previous and next in the listening room. The needle lifts and comes down by itself, so nothing gets scratched.
Previous and next in the listening room, straight to the song, with no wait for winding and no creases.
The vinyl under the music, for records from a folder. It grows with wear.
The tape under the music, for albums from a folder. It grows with wear.
Its own: records live in a dark room.
Its own: cassettes live in daylight.
A recorded crackle instead of the made-up one, under folder records and over your streaming app too.
A recorded tape hiss instead of the made-up one, under folder albums and over your streaming app too.
Start albums in Spotify without opening it
Optional. Spotify only takes “play this album” from apps it knows, so you register Side A with Spotify yourself, free, in two minutes. Your Client ID stays on this phone.
1. Sign in to Spotify’s developer dashboard and choose “Create app”. Any name will do.
2. In the app’s settings, add these (tap to copy):
Under “Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?”, tick Android.
3. Copy the app’s Client ID here and connect. Spotify asks once for your permission.
Connected. “Play the album” now starts it in Spotify quietly.
Not set: “Play the album” opens Spotify’s search instead.
Saved. Tap Connect to allow it in Spotify.
Spotify isn’t installed on this phone.
Starting a chosen album needs Spotify Premium. A record learns its Spotify address the first time it plays there; until then the search opens.
Spotify doesn’t know this record’s address yet, so its search opened. Play the album there once and next time it starts from here.
Spotify didn’t connect (%s), so its search opened. On Xiaomi phones, allow Side A to start Spotify when asked.
Recently played, your library and picks, without opening Spotify.
Spotify didn’t answer (%s). Check the connection in Settings → Spotify.
Listening along with a streaming app
Some phones stop apps to save battery
Side A has no account, no ads and no internet permission. Your shelf, notes and listening stay on this phone. Music isn’t sold or streamed here: it’s yours, from your folders or your own player.
